title: Docker-compat /containers/json returns the literal string "<nil>" as Networks[].Gateway for a gatewayless network
body:
### Issue Description

On podman 5.8.2, the Docker-compatible `/containers/json` endpoint returns the
literal four-character string `<nil>` as `NetworkSettings.Networks.<name>.Gateway`
for any network whose stored configuration has no `gateway` key in its subnet.

`<nil>` is what Go's `net.IP(nil).String()` produces, so a nil `net.IP` is being
stringified into the JSON response rather than rendered as an empty value. It is
not a valid textual IP address in any form, so a client that parses the field as
an address fails on it.

The libpod endpoint (`/v5.0.0/libpod/containers/json`) is **not** affected — zero
occurrences of the string in the same state — so this looks specific to the
compat conversion layer rather than to how the network is stored.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Have a bridge network whose on-disk config carries a subnet with no gateway.
   In my case `/etc/containers/networks/<name>.json` contains:

   ```json
   {"subnets": [{"subnet": "10.89.20.0/24"}], "internal": true, "driver": "bridge"}
   ```

   Note the absence of a `gateway` key. `podman network inspect` renders it as
   `gateway=[<nil>]` too.

2. Start a container attached to that network.

3. Read the compat container list and grep the raw body:

   ```console
   # curl -s --unix-socket /run/podman/podman.sock \
       'http://d/v1.44/containers/json?all=1' | grep -o '<nil>' | wc -l
   10
   ```

   Each occurrence is a `Networks.<name>.Gateway` value. On this host there are
   five such networks and sixty containers, giving ten affected entries.

I could not reproduce this on podman 6.1.3: that version assigns a gateway to a
newly created internal network, and editing the stored JSON to drop the key does
not take effect, so I was unable to construct the gatewayless state there. The
affected networks on the 5.8.2 host were created by an older podman and carried
over in a host migration, which is probably why this has gone unreported — it
needs a network that predates automatic gateway assignment.

### Describe the results you received

```json
"Networks": {
  "<network-name>": {
    "Gateway": "<nil>",
    "IPAddress": "10.89.20.4",
    "IPPrefixLen": 24,
    ...
  }
}
```

### Describe the results you expected

An empty string, or the field omitted — some representation a client can parse
or skip. Anything other than Go's nil-pointer rendering.

### Why this matters in practice

Telegraf's `docker` input parses `Gateway` through `netip.ParseAddr`, and one
unparseable value aborts the whole `ContainerList` call. The result is that every
container's metrics stop, not just those on the affected networks:

```
E! [inputs.docker] Error in plugin: listing containers failed:
ParseAddr("<nil>"): unable to parse IP
```

Bisected against this host's socket, same config each time:

| telegraf | result |
|---|---|
| 1.38.4 | collects all 61 container series |
| 1.39.0 | 0 series, `ParseAddr("<nil>")` |
| 1.39.3 | 0 series, same |
| 1.40.0 | 0 series, same |
| 1.40.1 | 0 series, same |
| 1.40.2 | 0 series, same |
| 1.40.3 | 0 series, same |

Telegraf 1.39 moved this input to the official moby client, which is where the
strict address parsing came from. Telegraf is arguably too brittle here — one
bad field discarding sixty containers is poor robustness, and I will raise that
separately — but the field should not contain `<nil>` in the first place.

Container metrics were silently dead for two days on this host before anyone
noticed, because the collector stays up and the endpoint keeps answering.

### podman info output

```
podman version 5.8.2 (podman-5.8.2-12.el10_2, RHEL 10.2, rootful, netavark)
Api-Version advertised by /_ping: 1.44
```

### Additional information

Happy to run patches or extra queries against the affected host — since current
podman always assigns a gateway, reproducing this upstream may be awkward and I
have a live reproducer.

comments.body:
this should work fine with podman 6 already. https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28705

If you want to create a network without gateway you just need: `podman network create --disable-dns --internal int`

> {"subnets": [{"subnet": "10.89.20.0/24"}], "internal": true, "driver": "bridge"}

this is not a valid network content, no? Like we required the ID and name fields at least.
